market_holds: Spot about $8.03-8.15 on 2026-11-16 (sealed baseline 8.145 at 18:08 UTC; Yahoo daily bar 8.03 intraday), 9.5% above the 52-week low and 59% below the high. Front-week straddle 13.2%, event-implied move 8.7% after ordinary vol, ATM IV 142%, call skew (25d put minus call IV -18 vol points), put/call OI 0.26: options lean to the upside and are call-heavy (sealed baseline). Run-in: -15.7% over 5 sessions and -6.9% over 20, entirely in step with the quantum basket (from 2026-11-10 to 11-16 IONQ -24%, RGTI -25%, QBTS -16%, QUBT -17%, INFQ -14%; over a month INFQ has fallen LESS than every peer); today alone peers are down 5-8% and INFQ about 5% (Yahoo daily bars). Consensus: Q3 revenue about $11.05M and non-GAAP EPS about -$0.05 (Chartmill/Benzinga, undated snapshots); FY26 revenue $45.12M, exactly the company's $45.1M guide; FY27 revenue $55.8M (+24%); analyst data last updated 2026-11-03 (stockanalysis.com). Guide: FY26 about $45.1M after the Aug 17 restatement (H1 restated $23.4M, so H2 implied about $21.7M, about $10.8M a quarter, i.e. consensus Q3 sits on the guide's run rate). Positioning: short interest 30.1M shares, 15.4% of float, up from 25.1M the month before (stockanalysis.com, settlement date not shown). The line it trades on: not revenue. Q1 (record revenue, guide raised to $40M) fell about 11%, attributed to losses; Q2 (revenue beat consensus $10.6M by ~20-27%, guide raised to $43M) moved -1.5%. Management promised more detail on 2027 revenue visibility on this call.
view: Infleqtion is a $1.8B post-SPAC neutral-atom quantum name with about $520M+ of investments and cash, trading as a high-beta member of a quantum basket that has sold off about 20-25% since 2026-11-09 despite IonQ's big guide raise. Its own run-in is the basket's, not its own news: no company news since the Oct 29 date announcement other than small program releases, and over a month it has held up better than peers. On the print itself, the revenue line is likely fine: the company has beaten and raised on each print (guide $40M to $43M to $45.1M) and consensus Q3 of about $11M is just the guide's run rate, so a modest beat and a hold or nudge up of the FY guide is the base case. But two prints in a row the stock fell on record revenue and a raise, because this stock does not trade on revenue; it trades on the sector tape, losses and the forward story. The forward story here has two open items I could see and could not sign: (1) the 2027 visibility management promised, against a FY27 consensus of $55.8M while RPO was only $21M at Q2, roughly the H2 2026 revenue need, so 2027 needs bookings not yet disclosed; and (2) the $100M Commerce CHIPS LOI of May 21 has not been finalized publicly, while Rigetti (definitive agreement around 2026-09-08), IBM/Anderon (2026-09-17) and reportedly D-Wave finalized theirs in September; EDGAR shows no 8-K since Sep 24. That lag could be announced on the call (positive headline, with ~6% dilution at a 15% discount) or explained as a delay (negative). The company also reports on its 10-Q deadline day after filing an NT 10-Q for Q2 over a revenue-recognition error tied to a material weakness, a small tail risk. Overnight, an ordinary quantum-basket move is 5-8%, as large as the event-implied move. I cannot see which way the forward items land and nothing I found is stale in the price, so no call.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line (2027 visibility and the status of the Commerce award) is not visible before the release and I found no dated counterparty evidence that tips it; the revenue line is likely a beat but has not moved the stock in either prior print. The run-in is sector tape, which is not evidence about this release. Slight lean down only from the sell-the-news record (2 of 2) and the Commerce lag versus peers, too weak to bet.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A signed definitive Commerce agreement plus a 2027 revenue framework clearly above the $55.8M consensus would make up likely; an NT 10-Q, a further accounting revision, or 2027 commentary below consensus would make down likely.

self_critique: The case for up: the stock sits near its 52-week low after a basket washout, short interest rose to 15% of float, the options book is call-heavy, the revenue line has beaten every time, and management chose to promise 2027 visibility, which it would hardly do with weak numbers; a signed Commerce agreement announced with the print would be a clean positive headline. The case for down is stronger than I weight it if the sector slide simply continues overnight, since the quantum basket fell another 5-8% today. Neither is evidence I can date about the release itself, so 47 stays close to 50.
